en.askTitle: Put in your own offer, degree and family and get the same permit comparison and employer questions before you reply
en.runTitle: Casablanca to Lyon: a software engineer on a EUR 52,000 offer, with a pharmacist wife and a four-year-old

fields.label: Employer
fields.placeholder: e.g. a software company in Lyon

fields.label: Degree and where it was awarded
fields.value: A master’s from an école d’ingénieurs

en.template: Help me plan a move from {from} to {to} on a job offer of {salary} for {title} at {employer}, starting {start}. I hold {degree} and have {years}; my spouse is a {spouse} and we have {children}. Compare the Blue Card and the talent card routes against my salary, draft the written questions I should send the employer (innovative-company status, R&D link, contract type and length), rebuild the net pay, tax and monthly budget in EUR and MAD with my numbers, and mark anything unconfirmed. Ask before contacting anyone or paying anything.

phases.title: Read the official French pages on permits, fees, school and pay, and collect rents and rates
phases.note: Permit thresholds and fees, the family card, pharmacist recognition, pay and tax rules, Lyon rents
phases.judgment: Checking each route against his real salary and degree changed the answer. The Blue Card needs EUR 59,373 gross, EUR 7,373 above the offer, and the “qualified employee” talent card asks for a master’s obtained in France. So the guide points to the innovative-company talent card and tells him to ask the employer first.

phases.title: Write the guide, the budget and the source list
phases.note: Recommendation, permit comparison, pay and tax example, monthly budget in EUR and MAD

phases.title: Independent check of the figures and claims, then fixes
phases.judgment: The independent colleague re-did every money figure, and all matched. It still flagged a page footer that claimed a layout check which had not been written up, and a Lyon transport-pass price (EUR 75.90) with no source on file. The footer was corrected, the price stays labelled unconfirmed, and the colleague who built the guide re-ran the numbers after later edits.

workers: Compared the Blue Card and the talent cards from official pages: pay thresholds, who qualifies, fees, the family card and the application steps
Looked at school and canteen costs in Lyon, rent caps and example flats, and housing-aid eligibility
Rebuilt gross-to-net pay, income tax with the family quotient, and the euro–dirham rate from official pages
Mapped how his wife’s Moroccan pharmacy diploma could be recognised in France, step by step, and what health cover the family would have
Re-did every money figure on its own and checked the guide’s claims against the source list
